techniques.name: OmniVTA: Visuo-Tactile World Modeling for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
techniques.capability_it_enables: World-model-based visuo-tactile manipulation framework with a self-supervised tactile encoder, two-stream visuo-tactile world model predicting short-horizon contact evolution, contact-aware fusion policy, and 60Hz reflexive controller; built on OmniViTac dataset (21,000+ trajectories, 86 tasks).
techniques.code_url: WebSearch result block shows a GitHub repository titled 'MrSecant/OmniVTA: OmniVTA: Visuo-Tactile World Modeling for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation' at https://github.com/MrSecant/OmniVTA; result states 'The GitHub repository is available at: https://github.com/MrSecant/OmniVTA'.
techniques.verbatim_quote: OmniVTA is a world-model-based visuo-tactile manipulation framework that integrates four tightly coupled modules: a self-supervised tactile encoder, a two-stream visuo-tactile world model for predicting short-horizon contact evolution, a contact-aware fusion policy for action generation, and a 60Hz reflexive controller that corrects deviations between predicted and observed tactile signals in a closed loop.

techniques.name: Sound2Hap: Learning Audio-to-Vibrotactile Haptic Generation from Human Ratings
techniques.capability_it_enables: CNN-based autoencoder (CNN encoder + LSTM + residual vector quantization + SEANet decoder) that generates perceptually meaningful vibrotactile signals from diverse environmental sounds with low latency, trained on human ratings of 1,000 sounds.
techniques.code_url: WebSearch returned a GitHub repository 'Iris1215/Sound2Hap' (https://github.com/Iris1215/Sound2Hap); result block states 'the dataset, audio-to-vibration model, and web tool are open-source, with the audio-vibration dataset available on Hugging Face.'
techniques.verbatim_quote: Using this dataset, they trained Sound2Hap, a CNN-based autoencoder, to generate perceptually meaningful vibrations from diverse sounds with low latency.

techniques.name: Machine learning for smell: Ordinal odor strength prediction of molecular perfumery components
techniques.capability_it_enables: Curated ordinal odor-strength dataset of 2000+ molecules (odorless/low/medium/high) plus pipeline comparing multiple molecular encodings and supervised learners to predict odor strength directly from molecular structure for fragrance design.
techniques.code_url: WebSearch returned a GitHub repository 'peter-fichtelmann/odor-strength' with description 'Python code of the manuscript: Machine learning for smell: Ordinal odor strength prediction of molecular perfumery components' (https://github.com/peter-fichtelmann/odor-strength); result states the Python code v1.0 implements dataset curation, training and evaluation.
techniques.verbatim_quote: The code is available on GitHub at `peter-fichtelmann/odor-strength`.

techniques.name: kooplearn (Scikit-Learn Compatible Library for Evolution Operator Learning)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Unified scikit-learn-compatible library to learn Koopman/Transfer operators and infinitesimal generators from data via linear, kernel, and deep-learning (neural-network Koopman embedding) estimators with spectral decomposition; enables data-driven forecasting of nonlinear dynamics
techniques.code_url: Explicit GitHub repo https://github.com/Machine-Learning-Dynamical-Systems/kooplearn plus PyPI install ('pip install kooplearn'), readthedocs documentation, and a Releases page; representation-learning losses implemented in both PyTorch and JAX
techniques.verbatim_quote: kooplearn is a Python library to learn evolution operators — also known as Koopman or Transfer operators — from data. It is easy to use and strictly adheres to the scikit-learn API.
